Runic 2.7.0

  • Menu: a brand with International and China accounts (Kimi, z.ai, MiniMax, Qwen, StepFun) is one brand in the menu. The provider switcher shows one tab per brand; selecting it stacks a card per configured region, with an "Add China account" / "Add International account" row when one side has no key yet that opens Settings → Providers on that slot. The Overview groups the two regions under one brand header with INTL / CN rows and the same offer.
  • Menu: a new Resets panel lists every quota window that knows when it flips — across all providers on the Overview, or just the selected provider's windows on its card. Each row shows what's left, a live countdown, the wall-clock expiry ("tomorrow 9:00 AM", "Thu 4:30 PM"), and an elapsed ring for windows with a known length (5h session, 7d weekly). Ticks every 30s while the menu is open. Appears in both the popover and the classic NSMenu layout.
  • Resets: banked reset credits — the manual "reset my limit" allowance some providers grant — now show up wherever windows do. Codex reports the count in its usage payload and lists each credit with its expiry via the reset-credits endpoint; Runic reads both, so the Resets panel gets a "Banked" row per provider ("2 resets available · Full reset · expire Oct 4, Oct 5 · until Oct 5"), the provider card's session line says "2 banked resets · usable until Oct 5", the Overview row gets a "2 resets" pill, and the classic NSMenu gets the same line. The model is provider-neutral; Claude joins the moment its payload exposes the equivalent.
  • Codex: the additional_rate_limits block (a promotional model's own 5h/weekly allowance, e.g. GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark) is decoded and surfaced as the card's third window, labelled with the provider's limit name, so every window that resets is visible.
  • Claude: the OAuth usage payload's limits list is decoded; an active model-scoped weekly limit (a promotional model's own allowance) becomes the card's third window, labelled " weekly".
  • Menu: per-window reset lines on provider cards now carry both halves — "Resets in 2h 14m · 4:30 PM" — instead of only the countdown; the Overview row pill counts down live instead of echoing the provider's raw phrase. Providers that only hand over a phrase ("resets in 3h 12m", Gemini CLI) get it parsed into a real date so they join the countdowns.
  • Themes: Sumi (ink on washi — warm paper with visible fibre, sumi-black text in your chosen font, one vermilion seal accent, tapered brush-stroke rules, flat ink progress bars) and Blueprint (drafting table — cobalt paper ruled with a fine grid, crisp white linework, cyan drafting ink for the accent, Geist Mono numerals like dimension labels, title-block section headers; brand colors sit on cobalt like markers on a blueprint). Both are data-driven: theme JSON gains effects.texture / effects.textureOpacity (paper | grain | grid), chrome.borderStyle values ink and block, controls.progressStyle value flatBar, controls.chartSeries (themed | monochrome), and shape.separator values brush and rule.
  • Review renders: RUNIC_SCREENSHOT_DEMO=1 seeds representative quota windows into the screenshot process so Scripts/ship.sh renders show gauges, countdowns and the Resets panel instead of empty cards. Nothing is persisted.
  • Themes: Terminal repainted from green-phosphor CRT to operator console. True black, amber phosphor for everything the system says (brackets, selection, labels, progress), bone-white Geist Mono for every number, color reserved for status (green headroom, orange warning, red exhausted), scanlines at a whisper. Structure unchanged.
  • Themes: Relief — real light instead of paint. A warm desk-gray canvas; cards raised on a two-light shadow (a wide ambient plus a tight key from the top-left) with a rim highlight along the top edge; segmented pickers and progress tracks pressed in as recessed wells with the selected segment and the fill popping back up; buttons raised and pushed flat on press; cards lift on hover with springy motion; letterpress section headers; generous spacing so the shadows breathe. Driven by a new effects.elevation token in theme JSON, so any theme can turn it on.
  • Preferences: themed for real. Section headers use the same treatment as the menu (seal, brackets, rule, tracked caps), checkboxes are theme-owned on every opinionated theme, segmented pickers and buttons are Runic controls that take the theme's fill, stroke, radius, font and accent instead of the gray native ones, and the blurred mesh no longer paints a stray band under paper, film, or parchment. Terminal uses one family everywhere (Geist Mono, full size, calmer line rhythm) instead of mixing mono titles with system-font descriptions.
  • Themes: Light and Daybreak are retired — Light was System without the adaptivity, Daybreak was a palette with nothing structural behind it. Existing Light and Daybreak users land on Sumi; the older retired names map to their nearest living theme (nocturne → Blueprint, prism → Glass, pine → Retro). A short-lived Noir (film-noir monochrome) was tried during this cycle and replaced by Blueprint before release; the noir id migrates to Blueprint too.

Runic 0.14.0

  • Antigravity: new local provider for the Antigravity language server (Claude + Gemini quotas) with an experimental toggle; improved plan display + debug output; clearer not-running/port errors; hide account switch.
  • Status: poll Google Workspace incidents for Gemini + Antigravity; Status Page opens the Workspace status page.
  • Settings: add Providers tab; move cost usage + status toggles to General; keep display controls in Advanced.
  • Menu/UI: widen the menu for four providers; cards/charts adapt to menu width; tighten provider switcher/toggle spacing; keep menus refreshed while open.
  • Gemini: hide the dashboard action when unsupported.
  • Claude: fix Extra usage spend/limit units (cents); improve CLI probe stability; surface web session info in Debug.
  • OpenAI web: fix dashboard ghost overlay on desktop (WebKit keepalive window).
  • Debug: add a debug-lldb build mode for troubleshooting.
